Where to look: the levers ranked by dollars a year at the post's volumes.
A $40/MSF margin and a 3% trim target: contribution is priced beside, never added, and trim points over 3% become a lever.
Yesterday in the golden window: shift 1's operator downtime is over its 2.5% band.
The most maintenance downtime any shift has: a power outage plus jams; recurrence counts shift 2's own year.
A month: the five largest flags of many, each with its own trailing year.
Against each grade's target at the usual grade mix (the share of the setup clock over both months): the buckets add up to the gap taken directly.
Against the previous week: each loss is this week's feet below target per scheduled minute minus the week before's; an offset bucket is not priced.
Shift 3 against shift 1 over the same week: shift 1's Thursday planned maintenance makes stops an offset; the heavier grade mix of shift 3 is part of its gap.
